The words adhiśīlam etc. were orig. adverbs (adhi governing the second member, in a manner referring to …) and are still so used, e.g. adhiśīlaṃ (and adhicittaṃ, adhiprajñaṃ) śikṣā; loc. forms are also used in the same way, as adhicitte ca āyogaḥ = Pali (same text). These forms may be turned into adjectives: adhiśīlo vihāro; sa vihāraḥ adhicitta ity ucyate (this usage seems not recorded in Pali). Often the stems adhiśīla-, adhicitta-, adhiprajña- are used as prior members of cpds., in which case precise analysis becomes difficult; so;;;;; etc. But sometimes adhiprajñā-śikṣā is used as a cpd.,, the prior member being then evidently taken as stem of a noun. Pali saṃvattaniya, ˚ika; also prec. items), conducive (to, in a cpd., prec. by complement): dharmavyasana-˚nīyena karmābhisaṃskāreṇa, by performance of actions conducive to injury to the Doctrine; (ānantaryāṇi) narakakarma-˚nīyāni karmāṇi, deeds which conduce to deeds (leading to) hell; niraya-˚yaṃ karma; (karmāṇi) … apāya-˚yāni; karma alpāyuḥ-˚yaṃ, and long list of parallels in same ending; sarvajñatā-˚yaṃ kuśalamūlam; (Avalokiteśvarāya …) bahuparivāra-˚nīyāya (who is conducive to an ample retinue, sc., for his worshippers?); (dānaṃ dadāti mahātyāgabhoga-vipāka-)pratilābhasaṃvartanīyaṃ [Page540-b], conducive to attaining the fruition of …, and long list of such terms, all ending vipākapratilābha- (in line 9 lābha omitted by obvious error)-˚nīyam, qualifying some kind of dānam; kim asya dārakasya rājñaḥ ˚nīyāni karmāṇi na veti? paśyati, santi, has this boy deeds conducive (? conforming, suitable) to (becoming) a king or not? he saw, he has! (and the boy was made king); puṇyābhisaṃskāraṃ prasaved buddhajñāna-˚nīyam; here construable as adj. with puṇyābhi˚, but seems clearly subst. in (sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā) prasaved buddhajñāna-˚nīyam (what is conducive to Buddha-knowledge) aprameyam asaṃkhyeyam aparyantam; in absolute use, without indication of complement, ˚nīyaṃ kuśalamūlam upacinoti, he accumulates a root of merit conducive (to the proper result); seems to be used both as subst. and absolutely, without complement, in, (having lived in pleasure many years in the city of the kiṃnaras with their princess Manoharā,) sarvodyāneṣu ˚nīyaṃ (one ms. ˚nīye) anubhavitvā, having experienced what was ‘conducive’ (conforming, suitable, to be expected?) in all the parks, (he said to Manoharā).

, m., ˚ikā (to Skt. saṃvardhayati plus aka; one questionable occurrence in Skt., see), one who fosters, rears: sa te … kalyāṇamitra-janakas tathāgatakule ˚kaḥ; (bodhisattvānāṃ) vīryapāramitā ˚dhikā (both prose); ˚dhikā (like a mother) also.
, the verse-equivalent of Suvalitaratiprabhāsaśrī, q.v., in the prose story: ˚tākhyā duhitā (vs).

(nt.; to Skt. saṃvasati plus -ana; once in only), (co-)habitation, dwelling together (with, or in): dīrghordhva-˚na-saṃbhavaṃ (adj., originating in long dwelling in lofty surroundings) kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇam; (aparanta-, read ˚rānta-)-kalpa-bodhisattvacaryā-˚nena (involving, leading to, dwelling or association with the course of bodhisattvas of future ages) kalyāṇamitropasaṃkramaṇena; (sarvakalpabodhisattvacaryā-)-saṃvāsa-˚na-mahāpraṇidhāna-, great vow to dwell in association with …; sarvatathāgata-viṣayasaṃvasanena (adj., that involves dwelling in the realms of all Tathāgata) … ˚vihāreṇa.

, adj., and ˚cikā, subst. f., (to Skt. saṃ-vac- plus -aka, -ikā), in hasta-saṃ˚, ‘talking with the hands’, by signs (by or to the deaf): ˚cakaḥ (presumably personal) = Tib. lag brdaḥ byed pa, making hand signs (follows eḍamūka, q.v.); ˚cikā, subst. (the process), badhirāṃ ˚cikayārthaṃ grāhayati, by hand-conversation he makes the deaf understand the meaning.

, corrupt,; acc. to Index having lived among, but read some synonym of gatvā; perh. saṃcarya? The two passages are pratically identical: (vinipātaṃ na) gamiṣyati, kiṃ tarhi ( tu) devāṃś ca manuṣyāṃś ca saṃvācya ( gatvā) saṃsṛtya ( mss. saṃvṛtya) paścime bhave ( om. pa˚ bhave) paścime nikete … pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati. informs me that Tib. reads in mtshams sbyar ciṅ ḥkhor nas, normally = pratisaṃdhiṃ gṛhītvā saṃsṛtya (preceded by loc.), and in the same preceded by ñiṅ, for the two gerunds.]
, = saṃvara:; so also; see s.v. tāpa.
(nt.), some kind of medical treatment, perh. fumigation (lit. perfuming): … (snapanaṃ) ˚sanaṃ saṃvardhanaṃ varṇapariśodhanaṃ balasaṃjananaṃ prajānāmi.
(in Pali ˚saka, or ˚sa), see a-, nānā-, samāna-, steya-saṃ˚; also = samāna-saṃvāsika, q.v.: ātmānaṃ saṃvāsikaṃ sthāpayati.

(nt.; orig. ppp. of Skt. saṃvāhayati), one of the arts mastered by the Bodhisattva as prince: … mālyagranthane ˚hite maṇirāge …. Skt. saṃvāhana suggests shampooing; but acc. to Tib. rluṅ yab gyob pa, waving of fans.

(= Pali saṃvijjati = Skt. vidyate; is not justified in saying ‘esp. in questions and with neg.’), is found, exists; often virtually = asti: saṃvidyayanta (= ˚dyante,) ima āsana (vs); saṃvidyanta (read so, transposing daṇḍa before this) imāny … atiriktāny āsanāni, saced ākāṅkṣasi, niṣīda; mātṛgrāmo 'saṃvidyamāna-guṇo 'pi, even when no virtues exist (in them); puṇyasaṃbhāro na ˚te; ko 'smākam upāyaḥ ˚te; sthānam etan na ˚te, thatʼs out of the question, that canʼt be; with gen., like asti, = … has: yasyā ete guṇāḥ ˚yante, who possesses these qualities; (prabhūtaṃ me … koṣṭhāgāraṃ) ˚te, I have abundant …; (na ca me) … kiṃcit ˚te; na cāsmākaṃ svāmī ˚te, and we have no husband.

, ppp. (= Skt. *saṃvimṛṣṭa, cf. Pali vimaṭṭha), touched, mingled: svarṇaṃ yathā musaragalvaya (ʼs em., mss. musāragalva-, q.v., unmetr.; ˚vaya would imply an instr. sg. fem., ˚vayā, but no such gender occurs for the word; perh. read ˚lvaka, with -ka svārthe) saṃvimaṭṭhaṃ (so read with; ʼs mss. ˚māṣṭhaṃ; em. ˚mṛṣṭaṃ).
, ppp. (of Skt. *sam-vi-śvas-), completely put at ease or trusting: yadā jānetsuḥ tā rākṣasīyo, saṃviśvastā ime vāṇijakā asmābhir iti.

(sam plus vihe˚), injures: (nāgarājā …) mahābalo taṃ (better than ʼs so; one ms. lacks the syllable, the other reads va) ca na ˚ṭhaye (v.l. ˚ṭhayo; em. ˚ṭhyo, as if gerundive; jagatī meter) (vs), and I will not injure him.

, ppp. (of Skt. saṃ-vṛ-), (1) of a door, narrow (so, Chin., and Tib. dog;, shut): idaṃ khalu niveśanam ekapraveśaṃ saṃvṛta-dvāram eva; (2) (= Pali saṃvuta) restrained, controlled: ˚ta āyatanaiḥ = Tib. skye mched rnams bsdams pa (to sdom pa, used for saṃvara, q.v.), controlled as to the senses (āyatana 5); not by the senses; we might expect loc., but the instr. may be influenced by the surrounding phrases (visaṃyukto dhātubhiḥ, pracchinno granthaiḥ, vimuktaḥ paridāghaiḥ, etc.) where it seems more appropriate.
, n. of two former Buddhas:; (in otherwise quite different lists).

, f., (1) in the sense of saṃvara (1), noted only śīla-˚tiḥ; (2) (= Pali saṃmuti; see also sāṃvṛta), convention, general (popular) acceptance or belief; ‘common sense’; conditioned, exoteric, dependent, limited truth or knowledge, often in contrast with paramārtha (so also in Pali, e.g. saṃmuti mahārāja esā, ahan-ti mamāti, na paramattho eso); Tib. regularly kun rdzob, altogether void; may have been etym. understood sometimes as covering, but I have found no clear evidence for this (which is ʼs rendering, e.g., on) and believe it misleading; Pali saṃmuti suggests the true etym. (root man); cf. under (3) below: yāḥ kāścana saṃvṛtayo hi loke, sarvā hi tā munir nopaiti (vs, metr. deficient) = Pali, reading saṃmutiyo; defined as verbal symbols (prajñapti 4, q.v. for citation, as also for where saṃvṛti = nāmadheya, saṃketa, prajñapti); (laukikānāṃ … yasmin vastuni saṃketa-)-saṃvṛti-saṃstavanāgamapraviṣṭayā buddhyā darśanatulyatā bhavati, tad yathā pṛthivyāṃ, pṛthivy eveyaṃ nāgnir iti; saṃvṛtyā deśanā;, instruction according to ‘common sense’; ˚ti-jñānam (et al., see jñāna), common-sense knowledge, = Pali saṃmuti-ñāṇa, the fourth of four kinds of knowledge (as also in),, [Page541-b] last line, expl. comm. as any other kind of knowledge than the first three; asti saṃvṛtyā cakṣuḥ, the eye exists (only) in terms of limited, exoteric (common-sense) truth; similarly; saṃvṛti-vyavahāreṇa, by conventional terminology or exoteric (not fundamentally true) manner of speaking; saṃvṛtiparamārthataḥ, (knowing) both as to exoteric and esoteric truth; etāvac caitat jñeyam, yad uta saṃvṛtiḥ paramārthaś ca. tac ca Bhagavatā śūnyataḥ sudṛṣṭaṃ … tatra saṃvṛtir lokapracāratas (because it is, or, as that which is, current in the world) Tathāgatena dṛṣṭā; yaḥ punaḥ paramārthaḥ so 'nabhilāpyaḥ; katham anadhiṣṭhānā saṃvṛtir yuktā, kathaṃ punar ayuktā? yathā sati (text 'sati) sthāṇau puruṣabhrāntiḥ; kasya punaḥ śūnyatāvādinaḥ paramārthataḥ sthāṇuḥ siddho, yadāśrayāt puruṣabhrāntiḥ syād? (completely wrong), how may common-sense, which is without any sound basis, be right, and how on the other hand wrong? As, given a post, the delusion (occurs) that it is a man. But how, for one who believes in voidness, can in real (esoteric) truth the post be a fact, on the basis of which the delusion that it is a man might arise?; saṃvṛti-satya, common-sense truth, contrasted with paramārtha-s˚, (Tib. kun rdzob kyi bden pa); (dve satye); (dvividhaṃ satyam; but 17 has just said, avitathārthena tāvad ekam eva satyaṃ, na dvitīyam asti; this, of course, is paramārtha-s˚);; the cpd. saṃmuti-sacca is cited from a late Pali text in, and from by, but this last is an error (does the cpd. occur in older Pali?); saṃvṛti-saṃgha,;, defined as one in which all members are pṛthagjanakalyāṇaka, q.v., and in which () it is possible that a rite may be performed incorrectly in all innocence, hence conditioned assembly (of monks), where intentions are good but not necessarily results; (3) consent in the sense of a formal vote (of the saṃgha): yāni punas tāni (kulāni) śaikṣa-saṃvṛti-saṃmatāni …, families which have been held by formal declaration to be śaikṣa; so Chin.; note association of saṃvṛti with saṃmata (etym.!); samagreṇa ca bhikṣuṇīsaṃghena avandanārhasaṃvṛtyā saṃmataḥ and (an expelled monk) who by the entire congregation of nuns has been judged by formal vote that he is unworthy to be saluted; does Pali saṃmuti have this mg.? for such passages as bhikkhu-saṃmutiyā the Dictt. and give by permission of the (order of) monks, which here at least is possible; this, rather than vote (but the saṃgha did in fact vote on the question!), may be the meaning in brahmacaryopasthāna-saṃvṛtiṃ yācitavyā, she must be made to ask for permission (or, for a vote, sc. that she be allowed) to enter the religious life; so, āryikā-saṃghāt ˚tiṃ yāce ib., (the initiate says) I ask (this) permission (or vote) from the assembly of venerable nuns. Both and associate saṃvṛti (Pali saṃmuti) with saṃmata, suggesting that. ˚vṛti is hyper-Skt. for Pali ˚muti.

, ppp.-adj. (also, but erroneously, written saṃvṛta), rounded, in su-saṃvṛtta-skandha, with well-rounded shoulders, the 20th lakṣaṇa (q.v.): (Tib. śin tu zlum pa, well-rounded), etc.; Pali sama-vatta-.
, nt. (Skt. only m.), perturbation: mahāntaṃ saṃvegam (nom. sg.) utpannaṃ; but mss. vegaṃ, em.; vega, also, is only m. in Skt.]
, gdve. (= Pali id., to saṃvejeti, see next two), to be shuddered at: ˚yaṃ sthānam; ˚yāṃ … dharmyāṃ kathāṃ.
, ppp. (= Pali id., to saṃvejeti; caus. not in Skt.), agitated: ˚ta-mānaso (prose). Cf. prec. two.
, adj. (to Skt. saṃveda, or to saṃvedayati or saṃvetti), being aware of, experiencing: Vītaśokasya … vimuktiprītisukha-˚naḥ.

(cf. vedhati and Skt. saṃ-vyath-; Pali ppp. saṃvedhita), shakes (severely), intrans.: mahāpṛthivī … vedhe saṃvedhe (so mss., em. pravedhe; aor.) saṃpravedhe; the mss. of supported by (lokadhātuḥ …) vedhati saṃvedhati saṃpravedhati.
(= Pali saṃvohār˚; prob. denom. to Pali saṃvohāra, Skt. saṃvyavahāra), carries on business: baṇigdharmaṇā ˚ramāṇaḥ (cf. Pali). See next.
, adj. (to Skt. ˚ra plus -in, or to prec.), carrying on business: (mahāsamudre) pota-˚riṇa āsan; (here text ˚saṃhāriṇa, certainly corruption for ˚saṃvyava˚), 14, 17.

, ppp. (of Skt. ˚bdayati, used like Skt. śabdyate, is named, is called by name; Calc. ayam ehīti saṃśabdya means calling him by name with the words, Come, so-and-so!; but, to be sure, the true reading is śabdena, Crit. ed.), named, called by name: yena nāmnā ˚taṃ bhavati buddhakṣetraṃ; (tathāgatagarbho, line 9) ālayavijñāna-˚dito, as called by the name ālayavi˚; (cittacaittakalāpo) vikalpa-˚ditaḥ pravartamānaḥ, (mind and the mass of mental things,) being called by (that) name thru false discrimination …
, adj. (Skt. ˚mayati plus -aka), allaying, pacifying (plagues): upadravopasarga-˚kāni mantrapadāni; -upadrava-˚kānāṃ … mantrāṇām.
, by ʼs em., assumed to be adj. to saṃśaya, doubtful: (vs); better read, substantially with best ms., (sudurbalā, with ms. F?) matir iva saṃśayo 'tra me.]

(cf. Skt. saṃśīlana, and śīlayati), associate, companion, in monkish life: tatra dvau bhikṣū ˚likau, and taṃ ˚lika-bhikṣuṃ 4; so ʼs plausible em., ms. ˚śītika, which seems senseless; Tib. mdzaḥ, friend.

, or ˚la (if correct, related to Skt. śṛṅkhalā, ˚la, chain, with loss of nasal m.c.; some mss. ˚śṛṅkh˚, many with Calc. om. saṃ, both unmetr.), chain, as an ornament: maṇihāramuktahārāṃ mukhapuṣpake (final short!) ardhacandra ˚lāḥ (vs); text uncertain; Tib. () seṅ ge (lion) śiṅ lo (tree-leaf) ris (form); or does Tib. confusedly represent an attempt at transliteration?
, adj. (to Skt. ˚ṣayati plus -aka), drying up (trans.), fig. destroying (misery): -duḥkha-˚kaḥ (prose).
, m. = śrāv˚, q.v.: ye cāpi ˚kā tadāsī te śrāvakā teṣa jināna sarve (vs).

, prob. an sich heranziehen, as in Skt., s.v. śliṣ with sam, caus., 3: evaṃ ca taṃ bhartsiya (so read with v.l. and) tasmi kāle ˚yet taṃ punar eva paṇḍitaḥ (vs), and thus (the father) having scolded him (the son) at that time, he yet again would attach him to himself skillfully; embrace; conciliate; Tib. rab tu dkris, a lit. rendering, completely enwrap.)
, adj. (to Skt. ˚kta plus -ka, perh. pej.), (wretchedly?) enmeshed, entangled: vanagahanajāla-˚kānām apy ahaṃ sattvānām … samyag-gamana-(text ˚namana-)patha-darśayitrī bhavāmi; prose).

(MIndic for Skt. sraṃs˚; only noted Lex. and Gr. in Pkt., not in Pali), falls away: na ca vīryāta (so read) saṃsati (vs), and he does not fall away from his heroic stand (in practising austerities); missed by.
, adj. (m.c. for Skt. ˚sārin), involved in the round of rebirths: saṃsāre bahukāla-saṃsarī (n. pl.; no v.l.) duḥkhamūle (read dukha˚) (vs).

(nt.; n. act. in -ana to Pali saṃsādeti, leaves unanswered, so not only but also and, which defines wrongly; opp. of vissajjeti, answers a question), ‘letting drop’, leaving unanswered (a question): praśna-˚nena.
(caus. of saṃ-sad-), fells, strikes down: (sc. vanamṛgān) saṃsādya (ger.) … vyāghrāḥ … (vs).
, n. of a householderʼs son of Śrāvastī:
, adj. (= AMg. saṃsāriya: MIndic, or possibly error, for Skt. sāṃ˚), relating to the round of rebirths: -˚ka-citta- (prose).

(nt.), or ˚nā (= Pali ˚na; formed like utsīdana, q.v.), sinking: (of a ship) jale ˚na-bhayam; sarvasaṃsārasaṃsīdanabhayāni (sc. sattvānām);, understand a-saṃ˚, (anivartyacittā-)-saṃsīdanacittā, with mind not characterized by sinking; kā … bodhisattvasyāntarā vyadhvani saṃsīdanā; nāpy asya ˚nā bhavati.
, n. of a mountain: ˚ṭa-mahāsaṃsṛṣṭau, dual dvandva,.

, m. (= Pali saṃkhāra; both mgs. clearly foreshadowed in Skt., but here technically specialized), (1) usually pl., predisposition(s), the effect of past deeds and experience as conditioniṇg a new state: the fourth of the (upādāna-)skandha, qq.v., and the second item in the pratītya-samutpāda, q.v. (arising from avidyā, and cause of vijñāna); all as in Pali; for a brief and illuminating statement see; Skt. uses the word in virtually the same mg., s.v. 5; saṃskāra-duḥkhatā, see duḥkhatā; samskārahetu dadate na ca saṃkramo 'sti, vijñānam udbhavati saṃkramaṇaṃ pratītya (vss), it (sc. avidyā, in prec. line) furnishes the cause for the predisposition(s) and so (once avidyā is gone) there is no transmigration; vijñāna (the next link after saṃskāra) arises (only) in dependence on transmigration; (2) pl., conditionings, conditioned states, which means collectively the dharma (4) or states of (normal, sentient) being, cf. saṃskṛta: sarvasaṃskārā anityāḥ (as in Pali, s.v. anicca) sarvasaṃskārā duḥkhā sarvadharmā anātmānaḥ; kathaṃ ca bodhisattvaḥ sarva-˚rāṃ anityataḥ samanupaśyati; viraktaḥ sarva-˚reṣu sarva-˚ra-vītikramaṃ prāpayiṣyāmi; sarva-˚rāṇām … prahāṇāt prahāṇadhātur ity ucyate, sarva-˚rāṇāṃ virāgād virāgadhātur … (see dhātu 4); jīvita-˚rān adhiṣṭhāya āyuḥ-˚rān utsraṣṭum ārabdhaḥ, mastering, holding firmly, the conditionings of his life, he set about to renounce the conditionings of long-life, i.e. he determined not to enter nirvāṇa immediately, but to do so after three months, which would give him time to complete his necessary tasks; see (the term of three months,; so also Pali); Pali (after statement of his reasons) jīvita-saṃkhāraṃ adhiṭṭhāya vihareyyaṃ; comm. ˚raṃ ti, ettha jīvitam pi jīvitasaṅkhāro, yena jīvitaṃ saṅkharīyati, chijjamānaṃ ghaṭetvā ṭhapīyati; yo phalasamāpatti dhammo pi jīvitasaṅkhāro, so idha adhippeto; adhiṭṭhāyā ti adhitiṭṭhitvā pavattetvā jīvitā-(read ˚ta-?)-ṭhapanasamatthaṃ phalasamāpattiṃ samāpajjeyyan ti, ayam ettha saṅkhepattho; āyuḥsaṃskāra, conditionings of long-life, only as obj. of utsṛjati as Pali āyusaṃkhāra (‘usually pl.’,) of ossa(j)jati; ˚rān utsṛjati; ˚ram (text with 2 mss., read ˚rām = ˚rān with 4 mss.) utsṛjantānāṃ (sc. Buddhānāṃ; pūrvā koṭī na prajñāyate) (vs; next line, [Page543-a] nirvāyantānāṃ, mss. ˚vāpaya˚, vīrāṇāṃ p˚ k˚ na pra˚); bhava-saṃskāra = āyuḥ-saṃ˚; bhava-˚ram apotsṛjan muniḥ (vs), after samanantarotsṛṣṭesv āyuḥ- ˚reṣu 10, which follows above; same vs (also following āyusaṃkhāraṃ ossajji) in Pali bhavasaṃkhāraṃ avassajji muni; [in (vs) text lābhaślokau ca saṃskārau (most mss. ˚ro), but read (Skt.) satkāro = Pali sakkāra, honor, with same vs in Pali, supported by Tib. bkur sti = satkāra; cf. also lābha-satkāra-śloka.]

, ppp. (Skt. id., Pali saṃkhata), in the special sense belonging to saṃskāra (2), conditioned; in nt. substantially = saṃskāra (2): dṛṣṭījālaṃ uddharī ˚tātaḥ (vs), thou hast (wilt have) removed the net of wrong views from the conditioned (state of existence); similarly (vs); see anarthika for; tāny etāni catvāry api ˚ta-lakṣaṇāny abhisamasya saṃskārāṇāṃ samāsato dvayāvasthā-prabhāvitāni;, see s.v. avacara; the Buddhaʼs doctrine (dharma) is a-saṃskṛtaḥ (unconditioned) ṣaḍviṣayasamatikrāntaḥ (prose); prāpto mi dharmo hy amṛto 'saṃskṛtaḥ (read with v.l. asaṃ-, m.c.) (vs); uncertain, kalpākoṭī saṃskṛtā me anantā, bodhīmārgo śodhito me praṇītaḥ (vs), shortly after (above), but here Tib. ḥkhor bar (= saṃskṛtā; this Tib. word regularly = saṃsāra! whereas saṃskṛta is ḥdus byas in and, as regularly, etc., cf. ḥdu byed = saṃskāra; for Tib. … kalpas dʼune vie émigrante, for BHS … kalpas dans le monde de la transmigration, following Tib., and suggesting em. to saṃsṛtā in his, where he cites a v.l. saṃbhṛtā) bskal pa bye ba mthaḥ yas su, during endless crores of kalpas in succession? did saṃskṛtā here mean conditioned = in the conditioned state of life, as in ? or perhaps complete(d)?; applied to samādhi and the like as taught by the imperfect teacher Rudraka, ˚tānāṃ sāśravāṇāṃ … dhyānasamādhi-samāpattīnāṃ, and ˚ta-samādhīnām (asāratām upadarśayeyam), in contrast with the Bodhisattvaʼs own samādhi (sva-samādhi-guṇaviśeṣodbhāvanārthaṃ,); in this context conditioned (by the sentient world), not absolute, as perhaps in above.

, m., or ˚rika, only in tṛṇa-saṃ˚ (= Pali tiṇa-saṃtharaka; cf. Skt. saṃstara), mat or bed (of grass): eṣa te duhitus ˚rakaḥ; ˚rake (v.l. ˚rike) niṣaṇṇo; ˚rakaṃ upaviśetsuḥ; bhūmyāṃ ˚rike śayitavyaṃ, or … śayati.
, adj., in tṛṇa-saṃ˚ (cf. prec. and Skt. saṃstaraṇa; Pali saṃtharaṇaka-vāta), occupied with strewing or laying a (grass) bed: adrākṣīn Mākandikaḥ … Bhagavantaṃ ˚ṇakaṃ (prose).
(nt.; = Pali saṃthavana; Skt. saṃstava), intimate acquaintance, familiarity:, cited s.v. saṃvṛti.

, m., = Skt. as adj., intimate acquaintance, e.g. … jñāter vā saṃmodikasya (so read, see s.v.) vānyasya vā saṃstutasya kasyacit; so interpret, with bahubuddhaśatasahasrasaṃstutair (Bodhisattvaiḥ), who had been intimate with many … Buddhas;, praised by …; cf. also next.)

, m., and ˚ikā (= prec. plus, perhaps, specifying -ka), (one who is) an intimate acquaintance, friend: ˚takaḥ = Tib. smos (ḥ)drin, which prob. read for smon (ḥ)drin in both and; in a chapter headed mitrakāryam;; fem., of daughters of Māra, sukhakāraṇa devanarāṇa su-saṃtutikāḥ (see this; v.l. ˚saṃstu˚) (vs), here prob. endearing dim. -ka; (dve dārake) anyonya-˚tike kṣatriyadārikā brāhmaṇadārikā ca (prose); yathāsaṃstutikayā, adv., according as (you have) an intimate,.
, indicated by most mss. at, read prob. saṃstava; see s.v. saṃbhuva.]

, m. (otherwise recorded only, Kehrichthaufen acc. to comm., but reads sastūpaṃ and considers the word prob. corrupt; prob. related to stūpa in some way), collection, conglomeration: abhinnaḥ ˚paḥ (ep. of the Buddhaʼs dharma), a close-knit mass, = Tib. mi mthun pa med ciṅ (= abhinna) ḥdus pa daṅ ldan pa.

, m. (= Pali saṃthā˚; the noun saṃsthā does not seem to occur in an appropriate mg.), assembly hall, hall of meeting: (Śākyānāṃ) ˚ram upasaṃkrāntāḥ; (Śuddhodano …) Śākyagaṇena sārdhaṃ ˚re niṣaṇṇo 'bhūt; in the girls who are candidates for marriage with the Bodhisattva assemble there, while (18) Bodhisattvaḥ ˚ram upasaṃkramya bhadrāsane nyaṣīdat; in yena ˚ro … tenopasaṃkrāman (˚mat; text in 2 tenopā˚); ˚re (upāsakas gathered in it); (laymen of Kauśāmbī).

(nt.; cf. Skt. id.), determination, definition, establishment (of the Doctrine);, démonstration (good!);, exhortation (less likely): ˚naṃ kurvati Śākyasiṃho bhāṣiṣyate dharmasvabhāvamudrām (vs). Tib. yaṅ dag ḥjog, complete arrangement.

, nt. (in Skt. as ppp., and cited once as n., form, in from but prob. false reading; Crit. ed. pūrva-saṃsthitim, v.l. ˚tam; acc. to, Pkt. saṃṭhia, form), condition, state of existence: sukhenti sarvasattvānāṃ ˚tāni nareśvarāḥ (vs), make the conditions (of life) of all creatures happy.
, adj. (= Skt. ˚ta) ifc., formed, fashioned: prakṛtisvabhāva-sa˚ (prose). Cf. next.
, Bhvr. adj. f. (Skt. saṃsthiti plus -ka, or f. to ˚ta plus -ka, cf. prec.; with endearing dim. connotation), in su-saṃ˚, of fair form: vaya (daughters of Māra) … su-saṃsthitikāḥ (vs).
(= Skt. ˚sparśa; cf. spariśa and AMg. saṃpharisaṇa), touch, contact: ˚śena yeṣām ārogatāṃ … yānti (vs, m.c.).

(cf. Pkt. saṃphusiya, wiped away, clearly ppp. to this verb, altho it is not otherwise recorded in this mg. and derives the Pkt. from saṃmṛṣṭa, implausibly), wipes away, removes (?), or perh. (as in Skt.) comes in contact with, or (s.v. 6) masters, gets the better of: mitreṣu (6 putreṣu) ādīnavaṃ (read ˚va, with mss. in 6, both times) saṃspṛśanto eko care khaḍgaviṣāṇakalpo (vss); so mss., both times, surely to be kept (em. saṃmṛśanto, perhaps because of Pali saṃmasitā; but the two verses are otherwise quite different); the preceding, closely parallel vss have vijugupsamāno (viji˚, tu ju˚); translate, wiping away (removing), or coming in contact with, or overcoming, the evil (that resides) in friends (sons), one should …; the first seems most likely.

(Pali saṃsandati, caus. ˚deti, is similarly used, but Skt. only in lit. mg., flows together, unites), agrees (congruere,), with instr.: (arthenārthaḥ padena padaṃ vyañjanena vyañjanaṃ) ˚date sameti;; (bahujanena te, sc. dṛṣṭiḥ) … (na, added by em.) ˚diṣyati (em. supported by Tib.); dhātutaḥ sattvā(ḥ) ˚danta iti, creatures agree according to their dispositions (see dhātu 4); caus. ˚dayati, brings into association (in, loc.), or into agreement (with, instr.): taṃ sarvaṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ ˚dayati, yāni ca laukikāni śilpasthāna-karmasthānāni tāni sarvāṇi prajñāpāramitām āgamya (q.v.) dharmatayā ˚dayati, all that he unifies in the pra˚, and … these, owing to the pra˚, he reconciles (brings into agreement) with the standard.
, nt. (to prec. plus -ana; Pali samsandanā), [Page544-a] agreement: sūtrādi-˚naṃ buddhavacanatve hetur.

, ppp. (of saṃ-svid-, cf. AMg. saṃseyai; Skt. caus. saṃsvedayati, makes sweat, and cf. saṃsveda-ja,), moistened, softened (by boiling): tāṃ pakvamātrā saṃsvinnā (all mss.; cf. prec. line pacyanti; em. saṃkhinnā, which does not fit) khādenti (mss. ˚tā) sunakhā bahu (vs).

, in (iha janmani, see janman) saṃhartavyaḥ, acc. to,, cela doit être accepté, which is certainly wrong; prob. to be drawn back, withdrawn (because of an evil omen); acc. to Tib. brtul par bya (zhiṅ), perform expiation.

, adj. or subst. m. (to Skt. caus. of samhṛṣ- plus -aka), delighting, one who causes joy: catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ ˚kaḥ (saṃdarśakaḥ with one Nep. ms. of; Tib. does not support them) (prose); ˚kaś cā akilāsi nityaṃ (vs; no v.l.).
(n. act. in -anā, see prec.), a gladdening: (teṣāṃ … vaṇijānām) imāṃ saṃharṣaṇām akārṣīt (prose), made the following gladdening of those merchants (by gāthās now cited).

, adj. (gdve. to Skt. saṃ-hṛṣ-, or to prec. plus -īya), joyful; adv. ˚yaṃ, joyfully, in a way to cause joy: (mahāpṛthivī …) ˚yaṃ ca kampe, or (same with) kampayati;, the earth quaked in a joy-causing manner.

(m.; = Skt. or BHS saṃghāta, as such in Skt. but not in mg. 2;; not recorded in MIndic), (1) mass, collection: (Jīvakena vaidyarājena …) bhaiṣajyataru-saṃhāta-mayaṃ dārikārūpaṃ kṛtaṃ; sarvaratnayamaka-saṃhāto (Bhvr. adj., with kūṭāgāro 14); (2) in acchaṭā-˚ta, = acchaṭā-(q.v.)-saṃghāta: ekācchaṭā-˚ta-mātram api, for a single snap of the fingers (jiffy, trice).
, gdve. (to caus. of *saṃhārayati, MIndic for saṃbhārayati, denom., collects, gathers; see), to be caused to be gathered: (dhānyajātāni …) khalahāneṣu (q.v.) ˚tavyāni (prose).
adj. = Skt. sakala, all: … bhavet sakara iya mahī (vs), this whole earth would be …; only one ms. with Calc. sakala.
, adj. (= Pali id.), with duties still to be performed: aṣṭāham evābhūṣi śaikṣo ˚ṇīyo, navame (sc. day) yevājñām ārāgaye; hence, imperfect, failing in duties,.
, a kind of toy (not ‘game’), in a list beginning (akāyikā, q.v.) sakāyikā (n. pl.) vitkoṭikā … (v.l. saṃkāyikā).

, postpos. with gen., used in any sense pertaining to the abl. case; see, citing a Skt. case of mg. (1), none of mg. (2); (1) than: ayaṃ deva sarveṣāṃ sakāśād adhikataraṃ (more than all) pūjyate; asti sthavira tvatsakāśād anyo vṛddhataraḥ, is there any other older than you?; (2) because, on account (of): mahārāja tac caityaṃ na labhe brāhmaṇāṇāṃ sakāśād (on account of the brahmans) yathābhipretaṃ kārayitum.
, f. ˚nī (= Pali sakad-ā˚), ‘once-returning’, destined to have only one more incarnation (in this world, see):;; f. ˚nyaḥ, n. pl.,; ˚mi-phalam;, etc.; ˚miphalāni; etc. See s.v. srota-āpanna.

(= Pali id., Pkt. -sakkai, both apparently only in cpds.), in cpds. ava-(o-), pari-, perhaps anu- (see s.v. anuśakya), moves, goes. Derivation obscure; from ṣvaṣk-; Andersen, Pali Reader s.v. osakkati, from [Page544-b] sṛp (curiously, the mss. of read avasappanti in, see avasakkati).
(to -sakkati, q.v.), going, moving: koḍa- (= kroḍa-, cited by as the reading of Ḱ)-sakkino, moving on the breast (like reptiles).

, m. (= Skt. sakhi; analog. form based on acc. sg. Skt. sakhāy-am; cf. the stem sakhāra in Pali,; AMg. and general Pkt. sahāya is ambiguous; it could represent this as well as Skt. sahāya), friend: ˚yān dṛṣṭvā (prose); su-sakhāya-(in printed sa-sa˚) (-rakṣā ātmarakṣā ca kāryā); (-sametena … karmaṇā); susakhāyopetā apramattāḥ (all these prose); sakhāyair lakṣaṇopetaiḥ (vs).
(= Pali id.; ka svārthe, or endearing dim., to Skt. sakhī), friend (fem.): līlāṃ niśāmayatha he ˚kā = (vs).

, adj. (= Pali id.; cf. sākhilya and 1 akhila), soft, smooth, once of (a garment of) cloth: sakhilā khu-dayaṃ … karpāsānāṃ paṭapilotikasaṃghāṭī, mṛdukā-dayaṃ … (same words), masinā-d-ayaṃ …, sukhumā-dayaṃ …, tanukā-d-ayaṃ …, etc.,; this proves that the usual interpretation, friendly, cannot be right; it is of course based on the assumption of derivation from sakhi, but this is proved wrong by the passage; otherwise recorded in Pali and BHS only of speech, esp. the Buddhaʼs; in Pali regularly assoc. with saṇha = ślakṣṇa and mudu = mṛdu; sakhilo glossed muduvacano, and all comms. agree essentially on this, as well as on sākhalya, sākhalla (= sākhilya), which is the opposite of pharusa(-vācā etc.), e.g.;; sākhallena, glossed maṭṭhavacanena (note that maṭṭha is also applied to fine cloth, -sāṭaka); the mg. therefore is smooth, and of speech suave, mild, gentle: Buddhasya sakhilā girā (vs), repeated below; su-sakhila-ślakṣṇa-vākyo; sakhilā, in list of epithets of Buddhaʼs speech, = Tib. chub pa (? acc. to accomplished, perfected; Chin. seems to mean affecting the hearts of all creatures); of other (pious) persons, sūrataḥ (mss. su˚) sakhilo mṛduḥ (vs); su-sakhila-vācā (vs, by em.); saṃmodako sakhilo ślakṣṇavāco (mss. ˚cā) (vs). The etym. of the word is obscure; BHS akhila = paruṣa, harsh (of speech), suggests interpretation as sa-khila, but may of course be a case of popular etym.; no meaning of khila is known which would seem to fit.
, afflicted with hardness of heart (khila, q.v.): (vs; see kiṃcana).

(= Pali saṃkacchikā, surely not belt, waistcloth with; acc. to vest), an article of clothing, perhaps a kind of undershirt or shift: = Tib. rṅul gzan, sweat garment; Chin. a garment covering the armpits; (in a list of nunʼs garments) ˚kā adhiṣṭhātavyā (see adhitiṣṭhati 1); see also āsevaka, ˚kā.
(nt.), perh. rustling or the like, some sound made by water: apskandha-saṃkacchananirnādarutena (prose). Etym.? Perh. corrupt.

, ppp. (to *˚ṭī-karoti, to Skt. saṃkaṭa), pressed into a narrow space (of deer, by hunters), or endangered: tato rājñā caturaṅgeṇa balakāyena nirgatya tan mṛgayūthaṃ sarvaṃ ˚taṃ (by em., ms. om. saṃ).
(see s.v. kaṭṭati), collects, picks up: (… mālyaṃ vātena apakarṣīyate.) tāye dāni taṃ mālyaṃ saṃkaṭṭitvā (so, or v.l. saṃghaṭṭitvā, mss.; ˚kaḍḍh˚).

(nt.; Skt. saṃkampate plus -ana), a [Page545-a] shaking: gurubhāra-˚nā (so as one word, Bhvr.) Mārasenā jitā (vs); pṛthivī-˚na-(earthquake)-nirnādarutena (prose); (taṃ lokadhātum apramāṇaiḥ) ˚nanayaiḥ saṃkampya (prose).

(see also śaṅkalā; AMg. saṅkala, ˚lā, ˚liyā; surely connected with Skt. śṛṅkhalā, ˚la; on k : kh see s.v. asthi-śakalā etc.), chain (so Chin. acc. to; Tib. ḥbrel, ib., joining, connexion); the rendering skeleton or heap of bones, given by for and, cannot be right, since only asthi-sa˚ has this mg.; on alleges support of Chin. and Tib. for mg. skeleton, but groups this with the other refs. under the same Tib. and Chin., as above: in used of the chain or concatenation of mutual interrelationship: saṃketamātram … anyonyāpekṣasaṃkalā; janyam arthaṃ na caivāsti pṛthak pratyaya-saṃkalāt; usually fem. forms, ˚lā n. sg., stem in comp.; ˚lāyā(ḥ) (śaṅk˚), 9, ˚lām 12, etc.; kṣaṇabheda-saṃkalābaddhāḥ; saṃkalā-buddhi-(mss., text ˚buddha- on basis of Tib. saṅs rgyas, but this is prob. an error; orig. possibly baddha ?)-bimbaṃ ca, cf., also in the vicinity of bimba, pudgala-nairātmya-bhāva-svasāmānya-bimbasaṃkalā-nityaduḥkhāśubhalakṣaṇābhiniveśa-pūrvakam evam idam lakṣaṇaṃ nānyatheti paśyataḥ; in both these saṃkalā can only mean chain, (causal) concatenation; cakrapeyāla(q.v.)-saṅkalāt, from the chain of …

, (1) see asthi-saṃ˚; (2) in, text, yat tatra (after a palace decorated with sandalwood had been built) saṃkalikā cūrṇaṃ cāvaśiṣṭaṃ tat piṣṭvā tatraiva pralepo dattaḥ; Index saṃkalikā-cūrṇaṃ as one word, shavings; better two words as in text, perh. sweepings and sandal-powder (saṃkalikā, heap, sc. of sweepings ?); perh. cf. Skt. Lex. saṃkara, see s.v. saṃkāra.

(acc. to MIndic pass. to Skt. saṃkalayati), is gathered together, assembled, united, of Buddhaʼs teaching: the mss. are corrupt and the line uncertain, but in prec. line read with mss. te hi no upavadeyur anudagrā (they would blame us as ignoble); then, acc. to, yadi na saṃkaliye (assumed to be 3 sg. opt.; mss. indicate ˚liya) śāsanaṃ śāstuḥ (these words also uncertain).

, m., = vikalpa, false discrimination: nimittaṃ nāma saṃkalpaḥ ( nāma-nimitta-saṃkalpāḥ) svabhāvadvayalakṣaṇam, samyagjñānaṃ hi tathatā ( ˚naṃ tathātvaṃ ca) pariniṣpannalakṣaṇam = (vss); saṃkalpa-kalpa-janitena ayonisena (bhavate avidya …), vs; there is no noun for the two instr. adj. to agree with, unless we separate saṃkalpa (as instr.,), by false discrimination produced by vain fancy, and superficial, (ignorance comes to be); or understand manasikāreṇa as suggested by ayonisena? Tib. kun rtog (= saṃkalpa) rtog pas (by kalpa) bskyed paḥi tshul bzhin ma yin pas, which perhaps supports the second alternative, as it seems to make -janitena modify ayonisena. (In, vs, read anyonyasaṃkalpasagauravāś, as one word, having respect for each otherʼs purposes.)
, adj. m., of vile conduct; synonym of, or variant for, śaṅkhasvara-samācāra, q.v.: (not in).

, m. (= Skt. Lex. and Pali id.; note Skt. Lex. saṃkara, id., but in dung), (1) primarily, dust, sweepings, refuse, rubbish: = Tib. phyag dar; tayā dārikayā gṛhaṃ saṃmṛjya … ˚raḥ choritaḥ; ˚ra-kūṭa (Pali id.), rubbish heap (see 2 below), (tair hastapādeṣu gṛhītvā ˚kūṭe kṣipto), 11; [Page545-b] saṃkārāvakare śukle (read so, or ˚kara-śukle, for text śaṃkārāpakare śuklaṃ) paṭe … (vs), on a cloth pure in regard to sweepings and rubbish (i.e. free from them); lumbinivanaṃ … vyapagatatṛṇa-reṇu-(read khāṇu-? see next)-pattra-saṃkāraṃ (vs); padminivanaṃ … (read)apagata-tṛṇa-khāṇu-pattra-saṃkāraṃ (so mss., except khāṇḍa for khāṇu, q.v.), and read so lumbinivanaṃ … (mss. ˚saṃkara, and again khāṇḍa for khāṇu); em. saṃskāraṃ and saṃkhāraṃ, respectively, for saṃkāraṃ in the last two; (2) seems to mean more specifically dung, perh. in ˚ra-kūṭa (cf. 1 above), dung-heap, privy(?): so 'medhyasthāneṣv evābhiramate saṃkārakūṭe jambāle (mss. jā˚) keśāṃl luñcati amedhyaṃ mukhe prakṣipati (? but jambāla simply mud, so perh. saṃkāra-k˚ rubbish-heap); and more especially in and (but Tib. renders phyag dar thruout), where saṃkāra-dhāna (Pali id.) seems to mean privy: ˚naṃ śodhayitavyaṃ; similarly; dharmān pratyavarān ˚dhānasadṛśān; ˚dhānam imu mahya pūtikam uccāraprasrāva-vināśitaṃ ca (vs), especially clear, stinking, foul with dung and urine; (vs); (3) perh. impurity in the sense of pariahhood, outcaste state, expulsion from caste: (vayaṃ tvāṃ) jñātimadhyād utkṣipāmaḥ, saṃkāraṃ pātayāmo; but mss. are not unanimous, and in same phrase it is alleged that they read salokānāṃ (! kept in text) for saṃkāraṃ; quite uncertain. Cf. saṃkirati.
, adj. or subst. nt.? (gdve. of saṃ-kirati?), acc. to Tib. (what is) mixed up, to be mixed, a mixture, or confused, disordered (ḥdres pa, ḥchod ba): ˚yam.

(in this sense only pass., is soiled, in Skt. saṃkīryate, saṃkīrṇa, and Pali saṃkīyate, saṃkiṇṇa), soils: dharaṇirajaḥ kramavarā(n) na saṃkirati (in mss. ˚varān apasaṃkramati, unmetr.) = (vs), the earth-dust does not soil their fair feet.
(to Skt. kilikilāyate,), makes happy noises together (with others): (mātṛgrāmeṇa sārdhaṃ) saṃkrīḍataḥ saṃkilikilāyamānasya; similarly; and (see s.v. saṃcagghati).

, in, text, tām eva agragaṇikāṃ ˚yanto śayito, presumably understood as went to bed thinking about that courtesan (and enjoyed her in dreams all night). The form is very dubious; it cannot = Pali saṃkīyati which is pass. to saṃkirati, q.v., and not connected with Pali saṅkati, Skt. śaṅkate (connects it with both at once!), Chap. 43, s.v. ? If our form is right, I can only understand it as a MIndic passive to Skt. caus. śaṅkayati, makes concerned; it would then mean, being made concerned with … There is a v.l. sakrīḍanto; read saṃkrīḍanto, amusing himself (in thoughts)?
, nt. (to next plus -ana), drawing in, retraction: = Tib. bskum pa.
(cf. Skt. saṃkocayati and saṃkucati; forms in kuñc- recorded with simplex and other preverbs, not with sam-), draws in, retracts: saṃkuñcitaṃ vā bāhuṃ prasārayet prasāritaṃ vā saṃkuñcayed;. See prec.
(cf. Skt. kuṭṭ-, not recorded with sam-), beating, pounding, or (prob.) rather an instrument for doing this: = Tib. (b)rduṅ ba; Chin. mallet. (Tib. could be either n. act. or instrument.)
(cf. Kusuma 2, and next three), n. of a Buddha: (prose); ˚māya ca Buddhāya (vs, hypermetric by one syllable).

Skt. id.; the Skt. mgs. sign, signal, and name, are also BHS; note esp. vaidya-saṃjñāṃ ghoṣayitvā, proclaiming the title of physician = saying that he was a physician; Pali saññā is used in most of the mgs. listed below; Tib. regularly ḥdu śes, a mechanically literal rendering), (1) awareness, consciousness, as a generalized faculty, fundamentally as in Skt.: cf. visaṃjña, unconscious (in a swoon, or the like) = Skt. id., e.g.; technical uses, see saṃjñāvedayita-(vedita-)-nirodha, naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana (˚nopaga); (2) not clearly distinguishable from prec., notion, conception, idea, of anything in the external world: the third of the five (upādāna-)skandha (as in Pali), see upādāna (sometimes rendered perception); when the Bodhisattva sat down at the bodhi-tree, he received (pratilabhati) at once five saṃjñā, ideas or impressions, viz. kṣema-s˚, sukha-, śubha-, hita-, and (fifthly) adya cāhaṃ anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhiṣyati (so mss., em. ˚ṣyaṃ ti), and similarly, where the fifth is substantially the same, the others being atīta-s˚, kṣema-, sukha-, aśakya- (neither passage explains the first four); aśubha-saṃjñā (= Pali asubha-saññā), conceptions of foul things which must be meditated on by monks, see s.v. aśubha-bhāvanā; often prec. in comp. by other words specifying the emotional or intellectual content of the saṃjñā, (na ca) anityasaṃjñā-bahulā viharanti, and (backsliders) dwell not abounding in the notion of the impermanence (of sentient existence, as they ought to); parikatha bhikṣu yadī na bhāra-saṃjñā (vs), speak, monk, if you are not conscious of a burden (in doing as I ask), wrongly on Skt. and Tib. (khur gyi ḥdu śes med na gsuṅs); in a neg., or impliedly or quasi-neg., expression, something like the very idea, thought, āhāra-saṃjñā ca na tatra bheṣyati anyatra dharme rati dhyānaprītiḥ (Nep. mss. jñāna˚) (vs), and there will be no thought or idea of food, other than delight in the Doctrine and joy in meditation; adhimāna-saṃjñāṃ ca vihāya sarvāṃ (vs), and abandoning every thought of pride; sukhaṃ vinaśyatī teṣāṃ sukha-saṃjñā ca naśyati (vs), … and the very notion of happiness was lost; tena ca mahatā duḥkhaskandhenābhyāhatā na duḥkhamanasikāra-saṃjñām utpādayanti, and, afflicted with that great mass of misery, they do not conceive the idea of putting their minds on misery [Page552-a] (it does not occur to them to consider the question of misery seriously); (3) developing out of prec. (cf. āhārasaṃjñā, above, which might perhaps be rendered interest in, inclination towards food; and cf. AMg. saṇṇā = manovṛtti, mental inclination,), interest in, purposeful thought about: in (the Bodhisattva replies to his fatherʼs attempt to interest him in women; read with mss.) yasya tāta strīsaṃjñā bhaveyā so atra rajyeyā …, father, whoever has ‘ideas’ about women, let him take pleasure in them; the king replies, tava kīdṛśī saṃjñā bhavati 13, what are your thoughts or ideas?, to which the prince replies, mamātra viparītasaṃjñā bhavati 14, I have the idea of the reverse, i.e. (as the sequel explains), that things are the opposite of what they seem; here saṃjñā belongs to 2 above; cf. viparīta-saṃjñin, s.v. saṃjñin (3); (4) in BHS esp. false notion, erroneous impression in the mind: in (vss, unmetr. in; see his note and on Calc.) read, iha hetudarśanād vai jitā mayā hetukās trayaḥ saṃjñāḥ, nityānitye saṃjñā sukhaduḥkha 'nātmani cātmani ca, … three false notions, (viz.) the notions about the permanent and impermanent, pleasure and pain, non-self and self; saṃjñā-graheṇa (by clinging to false notions) bālā dṛṣṭi-viparyāsa niśritā (vs); samjñākṛtamātram (a mere product of a false notion) idaṃ kaṇṭhako vahatīti vādiśārdūlaṃ (the gods held the horseʼs hoofs); saṃjñāsūtraṃ (the cord of …) uddharī saṃskṛtātaḥ (vs); vitarkamālā saṃjñāsūtreṣu granthitā (vs), the garland of doubt, strung on the cords of …; sattvānāṃ … saṃjñā-vikalpa-caritānāṃ, of creatures whose actions are characterized by false notions and vain imaginings; mṛgīye … taṃ prasrāvaṃ pānīya-saṃjñāya (instr., under the mistaken impression that is was water) pītaṃ, so, ˚saṃjñāye;; bhagavaṃ (mss. ˚vāṃ) mṛgasaṃjñena mayā etaṃ iṣu kṣiptaṃ, under the mistaken impression of (your being) a deer (cf. 5 below) I shot this arrow; krīḍāratiṃ ca janayec chubha-saṃjña-tāṃ ca (vs), … and a state of having a false notion of (its being) fine (also cf. 5); keṣa-cid … vartati saṃjñā, some have the false notion …, and so, keṣa-ci saṃjñā 25; (5) in comp. with a prec. noun or adj. (as in some cases under 4), the notion or idea or impression, opinion, that (something or someone) is (what the prior member of the cpd. means); esp. as object of utpādayati (cf., under 2 above) or a synonym, forms, conceives such an idea or opinion; the object of the idea is generally loc., sometimes gen. with antike, q.v., rarely acc., sometimes not expressed (understood from context): (tato imā asmākaṃ striyaḥ sarvakālaṃ) paribhavetsuḥ, tṛṇasaṃjñā pi na (mss. recorded as ta) utpādayetsuḥ (so read), then these our wives would always scorn us, would not even think we were worth a straw (lit. form a grass-blade-notion, sc. of us); śrotavyaṃ (read ˚vya, m.c.) buddhavacanaṃ dullabha-saṃjñām upajanetvā (vs), one must listen to the word of a Buddha, realizing that it is hard to find; (te … durlabhaprādurbhāvāms) tathāgatān viditvāścaryasaṃjñām utpādayiṣyanti śokasaṃjñām utpā˚, … will conceive the notion of surprise and sorrow, virtually = will be surprised and grieved; hīnasaṃjñā, a low (= unfavorable) opinion, (na tvayā …) ˚jñotpādayitavyā, and with loc. of object, mā hīnasaṃjñām utpādayiṣyasi tathāgate ca bodhisattveṣu ca tasmiṃś ca buddhakṣetre; the opposite is viśiṣṭa-s˚,, below; others with loc., śmaśāna-saṃjñāṃ (mss. ˚jño) janayate iṣṭikāsu (vs), forms the idea about women that they are (repulsive as) cemeteries; tāsu mātṛsaṃjñā upasthāpayitavyā bhaginīsaṃjñā duhitṛsaṃjñā, you must learn to think of them as if mothers, sisters, daughters; kiṇīkṛta-(q.v., so read)-saṃjñā bhaveyur na ca tathāgate durlabha-saṃjñām [Page552-b] utpādayeyuḥ, … and would not conceive the difficulty of finding a Tathāgata; the object is in gen. with antike (q.v.), naiṣa mamāntike viśiṣṭasaṃjño (Bhvr.) bhaven, he would not have a high opinion of me; (sarvatathāgatānāṃ) cāntike pitṛsaṃjñām utpādayati sarvabodhisattvānāṃ cāntike śāstṛsaṃjñām utpā˚; also (see antike); object is acc., svabhavanāni śmaśāna-saṃjñām utpādayām āsuḥ, (gods etc.) began to think of their own dwellings as cemeteries (i.e. repulsive; (= Pali saññā-vedayitanirodha, the condition of the 8th vimokkha, and of the 9th samāpatti or anupubbavihāra), suppression of consciousness and sensation, an advanced stage of trance: (˚vedita˚), as condition of 8th vimokṣa; the ninth and highest of the anupūrvavihāra(-samāpatti), q.v.; also abbreviated nirodha(-samāpatti), q.v.; (˚vedita˚), as a samāpatti; (˚vedayita-)˚dha-samāpattiyo ca spṛhayanti, one of the two reasons because of which Bodhisattvas ṣaṣṭhāyāṃ bhūmau vartamānāḥ saptamāyāṃ bhūmau vivartanti. , m. (= Pali sattāvāsa), abode of beings. Nine such are listed and in Pali; in both lists an example only (not an exhaustive enumeration) is cited under each ‘abode’. (cf. the Skt. mg. Absicht, s.v. 3, and saṃdhāya), (special, cryptic,) esoteric meaning, the ‘real’ meaning of a Buddhist text or doctrine, opp. to its prima facie or superficial meaning; perh. always in comp. with a word for speech, words, or the like; but see also saṃdhi (5); see ābhiprāyika, which, is right in relating to this; my note in is prob. misleading in regarding complete meaning as basic; Tib. regularly dgoṅs (te), meaning, intention, often preceded, sometimes replaced, by ldem po(r), in a riddlesome way; nevertheless the implication of the word is always fundamental, ‘real’ meaning, as is esp. shown by (prose) yat punar bhagavann asmābhir anupasthiteṣu bodhisattveṣu saṃdhābhāṣyaṃ bhagavato 'jānamānais tvaramāṇaiḥ prathamabhāṣitaiva tathāgatasya dharmadeśanā śrutvodgṛhītā, but in as much, Lord, as we, not knowing the Lordʼs words as He really intended them (esoterically, cryptically, Tib. ldem por dgoṅs te bśad pa), there being no bodhisattvas on hand, in our haste heard and accepted merely His prima-facie words; so, saṃdhā-bhāṣya (Tib. usually as above);;; (vs, Tib. ldem ṅag, omitting dgoṅs) and 8 (vs, Tib. as in but om. ldem por); and (vss); saṃdhā-bhāṣita (Tib. generally as in) (see below; ldem por om. in 3); (gsuṅs for bśad); (paramasaṃdhā-bhāṣita-vivaraṇo hy ayaṃ dharmaparyāyas);; saṃdhā-vacanehi, ˚naṃ, and 5 (here Tib. om. dgoṅs; in 4 ldem poḥi ṅag [= bśad or gsuṅs] rnams, riddle-words; in 5 ldem po ṅag); note Buddhaʼs words in [Page557-a] na sahasaiva sarvajñajñānaṃ saṃprakāśayāmi, I do not reveal the Omniscientʼs knowledge all at once, given as reason for his hearersʼ failure to understand saṃdhābhāṣitaṃ, since (3) … durvijñeyaṃ … tathāgatānāṃ … saṃdhābhāṣitam. (14) trayaḥ saṃdhayo bālānāṃ pṛthagjanānāṃ, the three attachments of vulgar fools, are (15) rāgo dveṣo mohaś ca, tṛṣṇā ca paunarbhavikī … (16) yāṃ saṃdhāya (being connected with which) gati-saṃdhayaḥ (the attachments to other destinies, see gati) prajāyante. tatra saṃdhi-saṃdhānaṃ (read ˚nāṃ with v.l.; so implied by) (17) sattvānāṃ gatipañcakaṃ (under these circumstances creatures who are attached to the attachments are subject to the five destinies). saṃdher vyucchedān (abl.) … na saṃdhir nāsaṃdhilakṣaṇaṃ prajñāyate (after the cutting off of attachment there is no attachment, nor is any visible sign of detachment perceptible); here follow the passages, cited s.v. saṃgati 2, in which it appears that saṃdhi, [Page558-a] esp. the three saṃdhayaḥ (above), are, or are correlated with, the three saṃgati, these two words being virtual synonyms in this use; after this, abhūtaparikalpo hi saṃdhi-lakṣaṇam ucyate (vs), for the mark of attachment (binding to rebirth) is false discrimination; badhyante svavikalpena bālāḥ saṃdhy-avipaścitāḥ (vs); vijñānaṃ pravartate 'nyagati-saṃdhau, the vi˚ ‘continues to evolve in another path of existence’ (, freely but in essence rightly); anyagati-saṃdhau also, and gati-saṃdhau.

(in mg. 1 = Pali samannāharati), (1) (the only mg. discovered in Pali; also to pay respect to, to honour, but in the passages cited the mg. is simply focus attention on, pay heed to, e.g. ˚haranti, comm. punappunaṃ manasikaronti) focuses the attention (on), pays heed (to), takes note (of); complement, when expressed, generally acc., rarely gen.; sometimes the complement is a quotation of thought, so that the verb means fixes oneʼs mind on (the thought …), virtually considers, realizes, or with a future makes up oneʼs mind (as follows), decides; with a question, considers (a problem); gen. complement, devate samanvāharāsya (concentrate your attention on him) yasya sakāśāt tāḍakaḥ kuñcikā ca gṛhītā; sā samanvāhartuṃ pravṛttā paśyati yāvat, kālagataḥ; asmākaṃ (but this form is also used as acc.!) rājā na ˚rati (prose), the king pays no heed to us (his harem; note, similar situation, vayaṃ ca na ˚hariṣyati, where vayaṃ is acc.); mama saparivārasya na tathā ˚hariṣyanti; (vyasanaprāpto 'ham) asmi na ca me (as acc.?) Bhagavān [Page564-b] ˚rati, foll. by, atha Bhagavān … (3) Ānandaṃ ˚rati; asmākam api ˚harethāḥ (prose), turn your thoughts to me too; but much more often acc., ˚harati sma … bodhisattvo Brahmāṇaṃ (prose), noticed, was aware of, or took notice of; (Bodhisattvaḥ …) sarvabuddhān ˚hṛtya (having turned his attention to …) sarvabuddhebhyaś ca namaskāraṃ kṛtvā; (nagaraṃ, see s.v. agocara); ˚hara Jetavanaṃ, concentrate (your mind) on the Jetavana (whereupon they immediately arrive there by magic); māṃ Bhagavān na ˚rati (same phrase with me, above); ˚hartum ātmanaḥ pūrvajātīḥ pravṛttaḥ; ˚hara … Rudrāyaṇaṃ, turn your attention to Rudrāyaṇa; divyena cakṣuṣā tān pretān ˚hartuṃ pravṛttaḥ; asmān api ˚harethāḥ (same with asmākam, above); ˚harantu māṃ Buddhāḥ; (Śrīr … taṃ) gṛhaṃ ˚hariṣyati; ˚haratu māṃ Tathāgataḥ; (āścaryaṃ yan mām ete) ˚haranti, itʼs a wonder that they notice me; (bālapṛthagjanān …) ˚harāpekṣasva, pay heed and give consideration to …; passive expressions, sarvatathāgata-˚hṛtaṃ (dharmacakraṃ), which has been the object of attention of all Tathāgata; (Śakreṇa …) ˚hṛto (v.l. ˚hṛtaṃ, better ? it, rather than he, was noted) yathā rājā Kuśo ātmānaṃ … māritukāmo; so dāni Śakreṇa … ˚hṛto; (people, bhojanāchādanena sarve, so read with mss. for ʼs em. sarvehi, ca utsavehi) ˚haritavyā, are to be looked after, attended to, with …; vyavalokayantu māṃ buddhāḥ ˚hṛta-cetasā (with minds attentive, sc. to me); (buddhair …) samanvāhriyate, is noted, attended to; ˚hṛtāḥ smaḥ Tathāgatena; buddhāsamanvāhṛtair, that have not been paid heed to by (any) Buddha; absolute, no object expressed, te (ṛṣayaḥ, who have been invited) ˚haritvā (taking note, paying heed) … ṛddhyā yajñavāṭaṃ gatāḥ; ˚haritvā (upon focussing their attention) ṛṣīṇāṃ jñānaṃ pravartati; tatas te Buddhā bhagavanto ˚haranti mahābodhisattvāś ca, the Buddhas … (who have just been invoked) then pay attention, heed (the call;, viennent, wrongly); samanvāharatāṃ, gen. pl. pres. pple.,, see s.v. samanvāhāra; ˚haratv āyuṣmā(n), pay heed!; sarvacetasā ˚hṛtya; (ārya bhrātā te kṛcchra-)-saṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ, ˚hareti (˚hara iti), give (the matter, or him) your attention! (the monk addressed then enters samādhi and saves his brother from a hurricane); a candidate for initiation into the order addresses his or her spiritual preceptor at the ceremony, samanvāhara (misprinted ˚hāra) ācārya, take note (of), pay heed (to me), Teacher!; ˚hara ācāryike; and in taking the nunʼs robes, ˚hara upādhyāyike 15a.1; or (see above) the complement, that on which attention is focussed, may be a statement, usually attributed to the thoughts of the subject: ˚haradhvaṃ, tasya bhagavato dhātūnāṃ pūjāṃ kariṣyāma iti, fix your minds on the thought, We will pay homage to the relics of that Lord; but the quoted statement may also be a question, ˚harati sma bhikṣavas (voc.) Tathāgataḥ, kutrāsāv etarhīti, ˚haraṃś cājñāsīd, adya trīṇy ahāni kālagatasyeti, the Tathāgata focused his mind on (the question), Where is he now? and doing so he knew, It is three days today since he died; so dāni ˚harati, kahiṃ so rājā …; so dāni ṛṣi ˚harati, amukaṃ kālaṃ maye (= mayā) adhimātraṃ … phalāni paribhuktāni …, the sage focused his mind on the thought, At that time I ate excessively, etc.; mayā pramattavihārāye (see s.v. vihāra 2) na ˚hṛtam, evaṃ duṣkarakārakā bodhisattvā, in my negligent state I did not focus on the thought that Bodhisattvaʼs perform such difficult feats; ˚harati, kim asau gāndhika utpannaḥ ?; occasionally, instead of a direct quotation, what the concentrated attention reveals is expressed by a clause with paśyati, [Page565-a] Pūrṇako ˚harati, paśyati Sthapakarṇikaṃ … saṃśayaprāptaṃ, Pūrṇaka focused his attention and saw that Sthapakarṇika was in danger; so ˚harati, paśyati taṃ … pravrajitaṃ; see also above; (2) (cf. above, where before a future verb, samanvāharati could perhaps be rendered determine, resolve, have a fixed intention) ger. ˚hṛtya, deliberately, with intention: (a Bodhisattva never speaks falsely even in sleep, svapnāntaragato 'pi …) kaḥ punar vādaḥ ˚hṛtya, how much less with deliberate intention!; see also a-samanvāharitvā, ˚hṛtya; (3) also as specialization of mg. 1, gives oneʼs attention to, so prepares, makes ready, makes: (bhagavato ca bhikṣusaṃghasya ca mahantaṃ) maṇḍalamālaṃ samanvāhara (cf. line 13 maṇḍalamālaṃ taṃ māpayiṣyaṃ, and where the order is carried out, and abhinirmiṇitvā is the term used); (divyo maṇḍalavāṭo) divyāsanaprajñaptir divya āhāraḥ samanvāhṛtaḥ (cf. maṇḍa-, read maṇḍala-, -vāṭaḥ kāritaḥ); see on these passages s.v. maṇḍalamāḍa.

, m. (cf. also a-sam˚; to prec.; = Pali samannāhāra), focusing of attention, concentration of the mind on something; = manasikāra, as in Pali, cf. tajjo samannāhāro, comm. cakkhuṃ ca rūpe ca paṭicca … uppajjamāna-manasikāro; corresp. passage in and tajja-manasikāraḥ ˚hāra-(˚haraṇa, q.v.)-kṛtyaṃ karoti, the mental concentration thereby produced does the job of focusing the attention; in () ˚hāram (acc.; in all these passages vijñāna is based on three things, the sense organ, its object, and the mental focusing or concentration); (-kāyapraṇāma-)-˚hāreṇa kāyabalaṃ dṛḍhīkurvāṇaḥ … (19) citta-manasikāraṃ gṛhṇan, and others in ff.; (teṣāṃ cānantaraṃ) samanvāhāras (text ˚haras, doubtless misprint) tasya bodhisattvasyāntike bhavati, samanvāharatāṃ (gen. pl. pres. pple.) ca jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate.
